source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: Amidst the bustling ER, a nurse swiftly moved between rows of gurneys, her voice urgent over the intercom. Dr. Lee scanned the charts before him, her eyes scanning the register of clinical urgency. As the waiting chairs filled, a woman clutched her husband's hand, her complaint loud enough to pierce the white noise. He nodded, his frustration palpable as he glanced at their wristbands. Forms cluttered the nurse’s desk, her pen scratching across them. Nurses darted in and out, tending to patients, their hands deftly guiding IV drips and monitors. A curtain parted, revealing a patient writhing in agony, her condition critical as the doctors worked frantically around her. In the background, the rhythmic beeping of machines echoed through the corridors.
